content.title: Media Innovation Centre concludes June webinar series
content.summary: The weekly webinar series focused on the impact of COVID-19 on the Kenyan economy

media.alt: Media Innovation Centre concludes June webinar series

content.text: The Aga Khan University's Media Innovation Center (MiC) held the last episode of its second instalment of the Understanding COVID-19 Webinar Series that ran through the month of June.

MiC Director, Ms Njoki Chege, said the second instalment of the series was aimed at being a resource centre for journalists, students, professors, politicians and organizations who want to understand the impact of COVID-19 on various sectors of the economy.

"The current pandemic has brought about a lot of changes in our daily lives," said Njoki, "as much as it is a health crisis, the pandemic has also affected other areas that most people are not really focusing on. Our webinar series takes a deep dive into these areas, to paint a picture of what we are facing and creating a resource centre for everyone, especially journalists covering the pandemic."
Ms Njoki highlighted the speakers lined up were thought leaders in their various fields of work who gave a candid view on the issues.

"Our speaker line up included Prof. Karuti Kanyinga, Director, Institute for Development Studies, University of Nairobi who tackled governance and accountability, and Phyllis Wakiaga, CEO, Kenya Association of Manufacturers who looked at the impact of COVID-19 on the manufacturing sector." added Njoki.

Other speakers included Ms Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director, Dr Carmen Nibigira, Workplace Learning and Tourism Expert at Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and Dr Habil Olaka, CEO, Kenya Bankers Association.

Aga Khan University Vice Provost and Interim Dean, Graduate School of Media and Communications, Dr Alex Awiti, noted the importance of this webinar series in providing crucial information that will help journalists in their reporting during the pandemic.

"The complexity of COVID-19 has forced us to practise social distance to avoid infection and spread of the virus. This has made it difficult to access certain thought leaders for interviews and admission to certain areas to retrieve information that is critical in creating stories and disseminating them," said Dr Awiti. "Our vision for this webinar, as an institution, is to help the legacy media and media start-ups easily access various thought leaders in the country and out of this, be able to create stories and shape conversations around COVID-19 and its impact in East Africa."

The first webinar series that ran in May was a success, with guests such as Siddharth Chatterjee, United Nations Resident Coordinator for Kenya, Prof Bitange Ndemo, ICT specialist currently teaching at the University of Nairobi and Prof Reena Shah, Head of Infectious Diseases at the Aga Khan University Hospital, Nairobi among other key influential leaders in the country.
